wu: Students stand in a circle. Teacher tosses a soft ball to a student and asks 'Who is this person?', pointing to a family photo. Student catches ball, says 'This is my brother. He is funny.' and tosses ball back.
wuAlt: Students draw 3 family members in 30 seconds, then hold up drawings and say 'This is my mother. She is kind.'
Teacher shows flashcards of family members (mother, father, sister, friend). Students race to shout the correct possessive phrase: 'That's my sister!'
pres: Teacher shows a large family tree poster with photos. Models sentences: 'My father is tall. He has got brown eyes. He is working in the garden now.' Elicits and drills key adjectives and present simple vs continuous with student volunteers.
presAlt: Teacher reads a short paragraph about a fictional family, underlining present simple and continuous verbs. Students repeat sentences with gestures (tap head for simple, wave arms for continuous).
Students sort adjective cards into 'always' (kind) and 'now' (eating) columns with teacher guidance.
prac: Students work in pairs. Each pair gets a set of family member cards with adjectives. They take turns: 'This is my uncle. He is funny. He is watching TV now.' Teacher monitors and corrects possessive 's and tense usage.
pracAlt: Students play 'Guess Who?' with family photos. One student describes a person ('She is tall. She is cooking.') and the other guesses who it is.
Teacher writes sentences on board with errors. Students race to correct them in teams, focusing on 's and tenses.
ls: Students listen to an audio recording of a boy describing his family. They fill in a simple chart with names and one adjective for each person, plus one continuous action (e.g., 'My sister is playing football now').
re: After break, students play 'Charades Family'. Teacher mimes a family action (e.g., cooking, sleeping, studying). Students shout 'He/She is ____ing!' to guess the continuous action.
prod: Students roleplay a cafe conversation. One is a waiter asking 'Tell me about your family?' The other describes 4 family members using both tenses. They must ask follow-up questions like 'Is he funny?'
rw: Students read a short text about a Moroccan family celebrating a holiday (e.g., Eid). They answer 3 true/false questions about the text, then write 2 sentences about their own family using present simple and continuous.
st: Teacher tells a simple story about a family's Green March celebration, using visuals. Students repeat key sentences. Close with: 'Today we described family personalities and actions. Thank you, class! Goodbye.'
g: Students mark adjectives on bingo cards as teacher calls them out, shouting 'Bingo!' when they get a line.
Teams race to write an adjective on the board for a family photo first.
Students sort sentence strips into simple/continuous piles in teams.
Students walk around asking 'Find someone who has got a sister.' and write names.
Students draw a family scene and label it with simple/continuous sentences.
diff: Fast finishers write a paragraph about their best friend using 5 adjectives and 2 continuous actions.
Support learners use a sentence frame: 'This is ___. He/She is _____. He/She is _____ing now.'
hw: Complete the family and friends worksheet from the library folder, filling in blanks with adjectives and correct tenses.
Write 4 sentences about your family: 2 simple, 2 continuous. Draw a picture.
Interview a family member about their day and write 3 sentences in present continuous.
tip: Use Moroccan family structures and holidays (like Eid or Green March) to make the theme culturally relevant and boost student engagement with familiar contexts.
